newsitem.title: GERMANY: German travel agents may seek consumer booking fee.
newsitem.headline: German travel agents may seek consumer booking fee.

text.p: German travel agents may turn to a consumer booking fee to make up for expected lost Deutsche Lufthansa revenue.
Agents could be put in serious financial difficulties by the airline's cut in commissions for domestic German ticket sales to five percent from nine percent, they warned.
Lufthansa said on Monday it aims to reduce sales distribution costs, mostly commission payments, by up to 100 million marks next year.
Klaus Laepple, president of the ASR independent travel agents association, made the call at a joint news conference with Lufthansa.
"The sinking of the inner-German commissions will put many agents into (financial) difficulties," he warned.
"If there is only five percent for inner-German sales, then we could consider why there should not be a consultation and reservations fee," he added.
The ASR believed a 40 marks consumer fee would be the right sum, he said.
Laepple said the first Lufthansa model presented to agents in November with a high minimum turnover for bonus payments would have left them "somewhere between Waterloo and Hiroshima".
Gerd Hesselmann, president of the DRV travel agents association, added: "The commissions model offers chances and contains risks, both for the airline and agents."
"We are not satisfied with the stage of the talks. We still think five percent for inner-German flights is not appropriate for the work of agents."
But he stressed: "We have succeeded in that the minimum turnover of 500,000 marks has been dropped and so this model is open to all."
Hesselmann said the DRV had no view at present on a possible consumer fee.
A German IATA travel agents meeting would probably be held in April to discuss how to proceed with the new commission model. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
